A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OSV, and their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. All supplied pages were readable. v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-to-video evaluations, FVD comparisons in Table 1, ablations in Table 2, and a user study in Figure 7.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and additionally reports GPU-memory measurements and DINOv2 feature-MSE results in Appendix B.1 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The stated TTS inference rule is substantially revised. v1 Eq. 11 directly composes two model evaluations; v2 Eq. 13 introduces intermediate re-noising, averages estimated residual noise with Gaussian noise, and adds final noise injection. This changes the mathematical sampling procedure, although the two-stage training framework, discriminator backbone, and training losses remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same image-to-video task and dataset cited to Nan et al. The change from OpenWebVid-1M to OpenVid-1M corrects the dataset name rather than adding coverage. The additional diagnostics do not establish a new dataset or distinct evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same SVD teacher, AnimateLCM, and reimplemented SF-V comparators. The qualitative comparisons and user-study display also retain their comparator membership. LADD's addition to Figure 3 and the discussion of UFOGen concern research positioning, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v1 specifies 20K stage-two iterations at 576×320; v2 reports increasing resolution for the final 10K iterations. Section 5 specifies 1024×768, while Table 2h specifies 1024×576, leaving an inconsistency. The VAE-decoder ablation also changes from an explicitly stage-one-only Baseline-4 to Baseline-3. These materially revise the reported training and ablation settings without establishing whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original ablation themes remain, with revised decoder and stage-two resolution comparisons. v2 newly includes latent-versus-pixel visualizations in Figure 8 and a feature-MSE diagnostic in Table 3 examining conditioning-image similarity and prediction-target matching during LGP and ACD. v1 mentions supplementary latent-space analysis but does not include that evidence in the supplied PDF.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty estimates. v2's disclosure of 30 user-study videos per model concerns sample size, not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1's scores are unchanged. Table 2e reverses the decoder-condition assignments of FVD 232.25 and 171.15, aligning them with the prose. Table 2h replaces the low-resolution row with a mixed-resolution schedule and changes the full-resolution score from 181.95 to 173.14; these should not be interpreted as an established same-setting improvement. v2 also adds feature-MSE results and GPU-memory figures of 35.8 GB for OSV versus 73.5 GB for SF-V.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem A.1 and a proof asserting an O((Δt)^p) approximation bound under Lipschitz and solver-error assumptions. New distribution-level formulations in Eqs. 11–12 and Appendix B.1 also argue that ACD's adversarial loss can vanish while LGP's remains positive under distribution mismatch. v1 contains no corresponding theorem or derivations.

C1.justification: The headline contributions and FVD claims remain: two-stage distillation, a latent-space discriminator, one-step generation, and optional refinement. v2 adds an explicit abstract and introduction claim that directly transferring image-diffusion acceleration methods to video creates important performance, memory, and collapse problems, sharpening the claimed motivation for OSV.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the explanations for separating LGP and ACD, using LoRA, extracting features from latents, and removing inference-time CFG. It also revises the resolution interpretation: v1 says higher resolution is unnecessary in stage two, whereas v2 recommends it because similar FVD can conceal low-motion failures. The limitations additionally identify blurred hand movements and report that four inference steps resolve the observed issue.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D disclose previously missing loss weights of 0.1, Huber constant 0.001, 14-frame training and testing, and a Conv2D/PixelShuffle upsampler with factor 4. v2 also documents LoRA merging at inference, shared SVD initialization and default sampling, and 30 videos per model with user voting. These substantially improve implementation and evaluation documentation; most are disclosures about retained components and experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including UFOGen, T2V-Turbo, distribution-matching distillation, and sub-pixel convolution. It expands the discussion of difficulties transferring image-generation acceleration to video and adds LADD to the architectural comparison. The main related-work organization and positioning against AnimateLCM and SF-V remain.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds numbered sections, local explanations, and an organized appendix, while revising the resolution discussion and limitations. Author, affiliation, terminology, and citation-style edits also occur, but the retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 3, adds Figures 8–9 and Table 3, expands Table 2h's display, and revises several captions. Existing plots and qualitative examples are largely retained and relocated within the revised formatting. The appendix adds a contents page and single-column mathematical presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the contradictory decoder labels in Table 2e, supplies important replication details, and explains concrete failure conditions more clearly. These provide useful gains in reproducibility and interpretation. The gains remain limited by inconsistent resolution reporting between Section 5 and Table 2h. Moreover, the new Appendix A proof does not justify dropping the j-dependent summation between Eqs. 26 and 27, so the added theory cannot be credited as a fully established guarantee.
